note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Solution-manifold structure of two-layer linear networks and its consequences for representational analysis

nodes.name: Networks are non-identifiable
nodes.description: Artificial and biological networks are typically non-identifiable: structurally distinct parametrisations implement the same input-output mapping, e.g. through neuron permutation and ReLU scale symmetries in overparametrised networks.

nodes.name: Linear networks have a solution manifold
nodes.description: Under a convex differentiable loss and a non-bottlenecked network, all local minima of a deep linear network are global and equivalent to single-layer linear regression, and the global solutions form a high-dimensional manifold.

nodes.name: Complete parametrisation of global solutions
nodes.description: The paper derives exact parametric equations (general linear solutions, GLS) for the full solution manifold of a two-layer linear network, without assuming data structure or a learning algorithm.

nodes.name: Four nested solution types
nodes.description: The manifold is partitioned into GLS, least-squares-norm-of-function solutions (LSS), minimal representation norm solutions (MRNS) and minimal weight norm solutions (MWNS), each progressively constraining the weights (MWNS most restrictive).

nodes.name: Function and representation dissociate
nodes.description: Hidden-layer representations can vary continuously along the solution manifold while the network output is unchanged, e.g. a GLS can be chosen so representations form the shape of an elephant.

nodes.name: Task-agnostic RSMs for GLS and LSS
nodes.description: GLS and LSS permit RSMs that depend on the specific choice of input weights (including irrelevant input directions), so they are task-agnostic, non-identifiable and non-comparable representations.

nodes.name: Unique task-specific RSMs
nodes.description: The RSM of MRNS is uniquely RSM=ONO^T and that of MWNS is uniquely X^T V S V^T X, both determined by training data and independent of input-weight choice; these are task-specific representations.

nodes.name: Linear predictivity driven by solution type
nodes.description: Linear predictivity (R2) between networks is governed predominantly by solution type rather than functional alignment, since task-agnostic higher-rank representations cannot be linearly predicted from lower-rank task-specific ones.

nodes.name: RSA reflects function only for unique RSMs
nodes.description: RSA correlations fluctuate unpredictably when task-agnostic solutions are involved, and RSA reliably reflects functional similarity only when constraints enforce unique RSMs; MWNS and MRNS differ from each other even within the same function.

nodes.name: Representational drift need not mean functional change
nodes.description: Because representations can change without changing function, an optimal linear decoder trained on an initial representation degrades rapidly along a random walk on the manifold, so drift may be reparametrisation within a functionally equivalent subspace.

nodes.name: Stability-plasticity dilemma may not apply at network level
nodes.description: Since many synapse and representation configurations implement the same function regardless of solution type, the stability-plasticity dilemma need not hold at the network level and isolated synaptic or representational changes do not suffice to infer function.

nodes.name: Input noise does not force task-specificity
nodes.description: Expected loss under i.i.d. input noise is exclusively minimised by LSS, which include MWNS as a subspace, so input-noise robustness does not constrain representations to be task-specific (Corollary 5.3).

nodes.name: Generalisation does not force task-specificity
nodes.description: The secondary (unseen-data) error is minimised by LSS plus a perturbation in unobserved null directions, so minimising secondary error permits task-agnostic solutions (Theorem 5.1).

nodes.name: Parameter noise selects task-specific solutions
nodes.description: Robustness to additive parameter noise selects solutions with task-specific representations, ensuring representational alignment (Theorem 5.4, Corollary 5.5).

nodes.name: Nonlinear networks show analogous freedom
nodes.description: In two-layer ReLU networks on MNIST, function-preserving transformations (permutation, scaling, nuisance, duplicate, input-null) expand minimal networks into non-minimal ones with task-agnostic RSMs; non-minimal ones degrade faster under parameter noise, input-null changes have no effect, and test error is not inflated at near-zero noise.

isolated_nodes.name: Related-work gap
isolated_nodes.description: Little analytical understanding exists of how a network's representation relates to its function, despite this being essential for any quantitative notion of functional similarity.

structural_reasoning: The solution-manifold characterisation underpins the dissociation claims, implications for neural data analysis, noise/generalisation analyses and nonlinear validation. One framing claim is isolated.
